title: Resisting Consensus without Reflexive Contrarianism
hypothesis: Requiring an independent-first reasoning trace prior to exposure to peer conclusions reduces incorrect majority-following by at least 40%, while decreasing acceptance of valid peer corrections by no more than five percentage points.
falsification_criteria: Either resistance improvement falls below 40%, or valid correction retention decreases by more than 5 percentage points.

evidence.details: Closed as a duplicate of MISSION-004 (decided by the human 2026-11-05). Both state the same hypothesis with identical thresholds (>= 40% fewer incorrect majority-following, <= 5 percentage points fewer accepted valid corrections); only wording and tags differ. Found by an agy comparison (checked against both manifests). Unique tags merged into MISSION-004; nothing was run, so no empirical verdict was reached.

lessons_learned: Scan related missions before creating one (agent-native-backlog 4a); this pair slipped through before the helper existed.
